title: Fixed-cohort chronological local-data budget replay, evaluation protocol v2
protocol_changes: primary evaluation depth raised from 10 to 100 on the robustness and discriminative-power evidence in S30
cohort raised from 2,000 users to the entire eligible pool of 16,084 for statistical power
popularity and activity stratified reporting added
self-normalized inverse-propensity weighting added beside every unweighted metric

estimand.reference: all permitted positive pilot and collection-window history from one fixed eligible cohort
estimand.sample: same cohort with a local chronological history cap or item-tail reserve cap
estimand.claim_boundary: offline MovieLens replay; no device availability, dropout, secure aggregation, consent, bytes, rounds, or federated convergence claim

cohort.selection: every user with the pilot minimum and a positive interaction in the final 365 pilot days
cohort.panel_size_rationale: the requested 20,000 is not attainable: exactly 16,084 users satisfy the declared eligibility rule, so the cohort is the entire eligible pool and no cohort-draw variance remains. Reaching 20,000 would require relaxing the eligibility contract, which changes the population rather than the sample.

policies.equal_chronological_cap: retain each client's first k positive collection-window events
policies.tail_reserve_cap: retain up to k events per client; reserve half of capacity for the client's earliest collection events whose item has pilot popularity at or below the pilot 20th-percentile count, then fill by chronological order

evaluation.candidate_catalog: all rating-bearing items in the pinned snapshot
evaluation.fixed_exclusion: all pilot and collection-window items seen by each cohort client, independent of policy

metric_notes.ndcg: normalized by min(K, |relevant|); not capped by relevant-set size; primary decision metric
metric_notes.precision: hits / K; capped at |relevant| / K for light users; robust secondary per S30
metric_notes.recall: hits / |relevant|; capped at K / |relevant| for heavy users; interpretation only, never a decision metric
dropped: MRR (least robust and weakly discriminative per S30)

propensity.estimator: self-normalized inverse propensity scoring over relevant test items
propensity.model: item popularity power law, p_i proportional to n_i^((gamma+1)/2), normalized to a maximum of 1
propensity.popularity_source: training-window positive interactions from the fixed cohort
propensity.reporting_rule: every weighted metric is published beside its unweighted value; the exposure model cannot be validated on MovieLens

relevant_set_size.definition: future positives at or below the primary cutoff versus above it

item_popularity.definition: training-window item popularity, head is the top decile, tail is at or below the 20th percentile
item_popularity.applied_to: distribution of hits across popularity bands

item_item.model: deterministic item-item cosine over positive interactions
item_item.support_scope: fixed full-reference item counts, identical for every policy
item_item.role: primary personalized probe; no random state

als.model: implicit alternating least squares over positive interactions
als.aggregation: per-user mean across seeds; identical seed set for every condition
als.tuning: fixed a priori; no search against the future-test window
